turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response: Well, I'm here because I've been having this issue where I just... lose chunks of time. I'll be getting ready to leave the house, or sitting down to start work, and I end up spending way too long re-reading emails and texts. Or I'll keep reopening folders on my computer to check them. And I do this thing where I mentally replay conversations over and over. It's like I have to prove to myself that I didn't make some kind of serious mistake. It's really starting to get in the way.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes engaging in repetitive behaviors (re-reading emails, reopening folders) and mental acts (replaying conversations) to prove they didn't make a mistake.

turns.doctor_question: What happens or what do you feel inside if you try to stop yourself from checking or replaying these things?
turns.patient_response:
I'm not exactly sure how to describe it. I just get really agitated. If I try to force myself to stop—like if I just close the email or try to move on to my actual work—I just can't focus. 

It feels like something is wrong or unfinished. My mind just keeps pulling me back to it, and that tense feeling doesn't really go away until I finally just give in and check it again.

turns.doctor_question: Deep down, do you feel that this level of checking makes logical sense, or does it feel excessive and irrational to you?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, I know it's excessive. It really doesn't make logical sense at all. 

Like I mentioned a minute ago, I'm losing whole chunks of time before I can even leave the house or start my work. I work with computers, so I know that reopening the same folders or re-reading the same emails and texts over and over isn't actually accomplishing anything. And mentally replaying those conversations just to prove to myself I didn't make some serious mistake... I know, logically, that I didn't do anything wrong. 

I know it's irrational. But I still get stuck doing it anyway.

turns.doctor_question: On a typical day, roughly how much total time would you say you spend on these checking behaviors and replaying conversations?
